title: Invertibility of the finite exceptional quotient mate
statement: Fix l prime, a finite extension E of Q_l, the finite-field datum D with l different from D.p, separated finite-type D.k-schemes X,Y, a separated finite-type morphism f:X→Y over D.k and a compactification c. Use the actual finite-Tor domains, normalized adjunctions and quotient mate b of [def-sf-finite-exceptional-constructions]. For every n≤m (indices denote positive exponents n+1 and m+1), the natural transformation b:G_m⋙Q_X→Q_Y⋙G_n is invertible.

source.place: Paragraph 2: coherent duality comparisons and identification of their adjunction maps

proof.text: Apply the finite Verdier coefficient comparison on X and Y, and commute quotient tensor past ordinary pullback. On V=f*D_Y L compose the X duality comparison with D_X of the inverse of the inner comparison t:Q_X V→f*D_Y Q_Y L. Each factor is an isomorphism and natural on the finite-Tor domain. Conjugate the resulting Q_X H_m→H_n Q_Y by the uniquely normalized dual formula at both levels.

Finite Hom coefficient change preserves evaluation. Absolute dualizing coefficient change preserves the structural trace, and compact-support coefficient change preserves the counit and projection. Therefore the transpose of the constructed comparison is q inverse followed by the quotient image of the old counit. The target adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so this comparison is exactly b. Its inverse is the reverse composite of the inverses; full-subcategory inclusion reflects invertibility.
